findings.title: Floating-point multiplication before rounding
findings.body: The calculation `totalCents(booking) * (percent / 100)` performs floating-point arithmetic, which can introduce tiny rounding errors before `Math.round` is applied. This may cause the final cents to be off by one when the result is converted to an integer. Use integer arithmetic or a fixed-point library to avoid precision loss.

findings.title: Unnecessary rounding before conversion to cents
findings.body: The value `rounded` is already an integer after `Math.round`, but `toCents` is called on it. If `toCents` is intended to handle rounding, this extra step is redundant. If `toCents` expects a float, it should be documented or renamed to clarify its purpose.

summary.problem: The new `depositCents` function risks precision loss due to floating-point arithmetic and performs an unnecessary rounding step before converting to cents.
summary.done_well: The function clearly separates the calculation, rounding, and conversion steps, and reuses existing utilities like `totalCents` and `toCents`.
